reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) strongly supports the mechanism of LCO enhancing irradiation resistance via defect mobility and recombination, but this evidence is exclusively for the CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy, not RHEAs. No cited evidence supports the introduction of LCO in RHEAs via thermal aging, its effect on mechanical performance, or its stability under high-temperature conditions. E4 and E5 are irrelevant to LCO.
premises: Local chemical order (LCO) can be introduced in refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) via thermal aging
LCO narrows the mobility ratio of irradiation-induced interstitials and vacancies, enhancing their recombination
This enhanced recombination improves irradiation resistance
Improved irradiation resistance translates to improved mechanical performance in RHEAs
LCO remains stable under high-temperature and irradiation conditions relevant to RHEA applications
